claims.text: The starting bulk CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous FCC structure.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi has low or acceptable friction at room temperature.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi experiences increased friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature degradation of uncoated CoCrFeNi is caused by surface softening, insufficient surface protection, and unstable oxide formation.
An ultrathin nanostructured oxide coating should be deposited by PVD on the CoCrFeNi surface.
Alumina or a similar oxide would provide high-temperature stability in the proposed coating.
The coating will possess a nanohierarchical architecture containing nano-coupled grains and/or nanoprecipitates.
At room temperature, the nanostructured architecture will dissipate or release frictional stress through multiple deformation pathways.
Room-temperature stress dissipation will occur without generating damaging wear particles.
At high temperature, the coating will undergo controlled tribo-oxidation and rapidly form a continuous, dense nanocrystalline glaze.
The high-temperature nanocrystalline glaze will minimize adhesive and oxidative wear.
The room-temperature stress-relief mechanism and high-temperature glaze mechanism together will maintain low friction and wear throughout 25–800 °C.
The coated CoCrFeNi will outperform uncoated CoCrFeNi in both coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range.
The coated alloy will maintain a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.2–0.3 from room temperature to 800 °C.
The coated alloy will maintain wear rates on the order of 10^-7 mm^3/Nm from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed performance domain is dry sliding in air from 25 °C to 800 °C under normal loads of approximately 5–20 N and typical tribometer sliding speeds.
Coating composition, thickness, and nanostructure must be optimized to balance room-temperature behavior with high-temperature glaze formation.
Variability in coating adhesion and scale-up to larger components may affect performance.
